daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The DPR is considering changing the nomenclature of the asset forfeiture bill to an "asset recovery" bill and establishing a new independent agency to handle the process. Commission III is reviewing proposals to rename the legislation, while DPR members believe the bill could be completed this year. Separately, Commission III affirmed it is fast-tracking the asset forfeiture bill using an accelerated process.

  • The Prosecutor's Office has transferred the corruption case against former Junior Attorney General for Special Crimes Febrie Adriansyah to its own jurisdiction, and is still investigating the ownership of gold and cash found at his Sentul residence.
  • Febrie Adriansyah remains a civil servant despite his resignation from the Jampidsus position and designation as a corruption suspect.
  • Defence Minister Sjafrie convened a meeting of the Anti-Corruption Task Force leadership, though the National Police Chief was notably absent.
  • PDI-P chair Megawati received the UAE Ambassador to discuss Middle East geopolitics and research cooperation, and separately met the South Korean Ambassador to discuss Korean peace efforts.
  • NU figure Gus Ipul urged NU members not to fall for hoaxes from online buzzers ahead of the organisation's national congress.
  • Commission III called on police to detain the head of an Islamic boarding school who is a suspect in the burning of a student.
  • The KPK will investigate corruption from the era of the husband of Sukoharjo Regent, describing the extortion pattern as "copy-paste".

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia's drug regulator BPOM is taking steps to mitigate potential disruptions to the pharmaceutical industry from the ongoing Strait of Hormuz crisis involving the United States and Iran. BPOM is implementing contingency measures to ensure continuity of medicine supplies as tensions escalate in the vital shipping lane. The Indonesian Ambassador to Saudi Arabia has assured that Saudi Arabia remains safe for Indonesian pilgrims despite the US-Iran escalation in the region.

  • Indian Prime Minister Modi's recent visit to Indonesia is being characterized as marking a new era for the Indonesia-India strategic partnership.
  • Indonesia's Transport Minister Dudy stated that Saudi Arabia is exploring investment in Indonesia's maritime transportation sector.
  • The Indonesian Embassy in Bogotá provided support to Indonesia's team at the International Physics Olympiad in Colombia, where Indonesia won five medals.
  • Australia and Indonesia launched Katalis 2.0 to support mutual prosperity between the two countries.
  • Indonesia's migrant worker protection agency P2MI is following up on the case of a Cianjur migrant worker repatriated from Libya.

Other

President Prabowo has approved a special subsidized fuel price of Rp 15,000 per liter for fishermen operating vessels between 30 and 200 gross tonnage. The special fuel pricing for fishermen aims to support the maritime sector, with the government formalizing the Rp 15,000 rate for eligible fishing vessels.

  • Financial services regulator OJK has issued new regulations on pension funds allowing lump-sum benefit payments under certain conditions.
  • Ratings agency S&P predicted the rupiah exchange rate will return to Rp 17,700 per US dollar, while separately affirming Indonesia's debt rating at BBB with economic policies deemed credible.
  • Indonesia has mandated the Coretax platform for all tax administration processes nationwide.
  • State energy company Pertamina imported 45,900 tons of LPG from the United States to secure domestic stock availability.
  • A minister warned that rising sea levels and land subsidence are putting Jakarta at critical risk of flooding.
